name: Whatever People Say I Am, That's What I'm Not

info.desc: Whatever People Say I Am, That's What I'm Not is the debut album by Sheffield band Arctic Monkeys, released on January 23, 2006. The album became the fastest-selling debut album in the UK since Definitely Maybe by Oasis. The album sold over 360,000 copies in its first week, but lost the title in November 2007 to Leona Lewis's album Spirit. It has since gone quadruple platinum in the UK and won the 2006 Mercury Prize. The album includes both tracks from the band's original EP, Five Minutes with Arctic Monkeys, as well as their first two singles and UK Number .

podcast.body: Often considered a masterpiece by critics, though some find it weak. The band's excessive creative freedom, combined with their inexperience, led to a lack of proper production. The album had two "producers" who were actually technical staff from Domino Records, and they merely executed the band's demands. This approach resulted in a fresh sound but introduced small technical production errors, stemming from the band's strong desire to avoid industry influence. "El primer disco de los artichmonks es posiblemente una obra maestra, al margen de que alguna gente lo considera un poco flojo."

podcast.body: Released on January 23rd, 2006, this album became the fastest-selling record in British history, moving 360,000 copies in its first seven days. It has since sold around 2 million copies in the UK and several million more worldwide. The album garnered significant critical acclaim, with two songs reaching number one on the UK charts, five music magazines naming it the year's Best Album, and winning the Mercury Prize for Best Album of 2006, Best International Album of the Year in Ireland, and two Brit Awards for Best Album and Best Group. Many of its tracks were re-recorded demos that had previously been shared online.

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This debut album was released in 2006 and became the fastest-selling debut album in UK history. Its remarkable success occurred despite all of its songs having been freely released online prior to its official launch. "And when their debut album, whatever people say I am, that's what I'm not, came out in 2006. It became the fastest selling debut album in the history of the UK, even though all the songs on the album had already been released online."
